Contrast SOC > ARB directly measures perception of socially relevant facial expressions (social interaction) in healthy adults using a group-level whole-brain fMRI contrast; meets global and local social-processing criteria.
Does not measure affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., kinship, cooperation, loved-one vs stranger). Missing local inclusion: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
SOC > ARB tests perception/reception of facial communication (socially relevant expressions) using whole-brain group contrast in healthy adults, satisfying social communication criteria.
Contrast measures social interaction generally rather than self-related processing; missing local inclusion PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 (does not target self-related perception).
SOC > ARB involves perceiving others' socially relevant facial expressions (understanding others) in a whole-brain group contrast, meeting perception-of-others criteria.
ARB > SOC specifically measures perception of arbitrary (non-social) facial movements rather than social processing; missing local inclusion SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2.
Does not measure affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., kinship, cooperation); missing local inclusion AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
ARB > SOC contrasts arbitrary, non-communicative facial movements (not social communication); missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Contrast targets low-level arbitrary facial motion rather than self-related perception; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
ARB > SOC emphasizes arbitrary movements (non-social) rather than perception/understanding of others' social states; missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
ME > OTHER contrasts self-involvement (being gazed at) versus observing others — a social-related task measured with a whole-brain group contrast; meets global and local social-processing criteria.
Task does not assess affiliation/attachment (e.g., kinship, loved-one vs stranger); missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
ME > OTHER manipulates gaze/ostensive signals (eye contact), a core aspect of social communication (reception/production of communicative signals) in a whole-brain group contrast.
ME > OTHER directly indexes self-related processing (personal involvement / being the object of gaze) using a whole-brain group contrast in healthy adults, satisfying perception-self criteria.
ME > OTHER specifically contrasts self-directed versus other-directed attention and primarily indexes self-relevance rather than perception/understanding of others; missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
OTHER > ME contrasts observing others (third-person) versus being involved — a social task measured with a whole-brain group contrast and therefore meets social-processing criteria.
Does not probe affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., cooperation, kinship); missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
OTHER > ME concerns perception of social interactions between others (reception of social/facial cues) measured with whole-brain group-level contrasts, satisfying social-communication criteria.
OTHER > ME indexes observation of others (third-person) rather than self-related perception; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
OTHER > ME directly measures perception/understanding of others (observing others' interactions) in a whole-brain group contrast, meeting perception-of-others criteria.
SOC × ME interaction isolates processes when social signals are directed to the participant (being socially involved) — a social-processing contrast tested with whole-brain group analysis.
Interaction does not target affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., kinship, cooperation); missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
SOC × ME examines social communicative signals when directed to self (reception of facial/ostensive cues) using a whole-brain group interaction contrast, satisfying social-communication criteria.
SOC × ME interaction specifically probes self-related processing in social contexts (how social signals affect self-involvement), meeting perception-self criteria in a whole-brain group contrast.
This interaction centers on self-directed social signals rather than perception/understanding of others per se; missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
SOC × OTHER interaction isolates processing of social signals directed to others (perception of others' social interactions) in a whole-brain group contrast and thus meets social-processing criteria.
SOC × OTHER does not assess affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., kinship, cooperation); missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

SOC × OTHER probes perception of social communicative signals when directed to others (reception of facial cues about third-party interactions) using whole-brain group-level contrasts, satisfying social-communication criteria.
SOC × OTHER focuses on processing of social signals directed to others rather than self-related perception; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
SOC × OTHER specifically measures perception/understanding of others' social signals (third-person social processing) in a whole-brain group contrast, meeting perception-of-others criteria.

Group-level whole-brain contrast of a live vs recorded social interaction task in healthy adults directly measures social processing (contingent interaction, joint attention components).

The task involves cooperative interactions but does not specifically measure affiliation or attachment constructs (no manipulation or contrast targeting bonding/attachment). Missing required local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1, AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
The live vs recorded contrast involves interactive gaze, instruction-following, and reciprocal exchanges (production/reception of facial/gaze cues), meeting criteria for social communication.
The contrast does not target self-related processes or self-evaluative judgments. Missing required local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1, PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Contrast isolates processing of another person's actions and intentions (e.g., pSTS, rTPJ activation), directly indexing perception and understanding of others.

Group-level whole-brain contrast from the same social interaction task (Recorded > Live) is a task-evoked map within a social paradigm and thus meets social processing inclusion criteria, even if reported activations are non-social motor regions.

The contrast does not specifically measure affiliation/attachment (no bonding or relationship manipulation). Missing required local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1, AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Contrast arises from a task involving interactive communicative behaviors (gaze, show/match events), so it meets criteria for social communication analyses.
This contrast does not probe self-related perception or judgments. Missing required local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1, PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Although reported activations for this direction emphasize motor areas, the contrast contrasts social conditions and therefore is part of assessing perception/understanding of others within the paradigm.
Joint Attention vs Solo Attention is a group-level whole-brain contrast in healthy adults directly targeting interactive social processes (joint attention).
The joint attention task isolates gaze-following and coordination, not affiliation/attachment per se. Missing required local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1, AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Joint Attention requires gaze following and reciprocal communicative behavior (production/reception of gaze/facial cues), meeting social communication criteria.
This contrast targets perception/understanding of others' gaze and intentions rather than self-related processing. Missing required local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1, PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
JA>SA explicitly probes understanding others' actions/intentions (gaze-following, pSTS/rTPJ engagement), satisfying perception-of-others criteria.
Solo Attention vs Joint Attention is a whole-brain task contrast within the social interaction paradigm and thus qualifies as measuring social processing (contrasting interactive conditions).
The contrast does not target affiliation or attachment constructs. Missing required local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1, AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

SA>JA contrasts a condition designed to minimize communicative gaze-following; it does not measure social communication (gaze-following) as the primary effect. Missing required local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1, SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
This contrast does not probe self-related perception or judgments. Missing required local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1, PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

SA>JA does not emphasize perception/understanding of others' intentions (it is the non-joint control); thus it does not meet perception-of-others inclusion criteria. Missing required local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1, PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.

Global criteria met (healthy adult sample; group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts). The analysis tests synchrony vs asynchrony in an interpersonal (social) task and therefore measures social processing.

This analysis reports the main effect of variance range (synchrony vs asynchrony) but does not directly measure or contrast affiliation/attachment (no affiliation-specific contrast). Missing local inclusion criterion: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

The task involves interpersonal synchrony but does not specifically assess social communication processes or contrasts (e.g., communicative exchange measures). Missing local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.

Although vmPFC was reported (interpreted as self-related), the analysis does not include an explicit self-related task/contrast or self-judgment measures. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Global criteria met and the contrast (synchrony vs asynchrony) indexes participants' perception of a partner's timing/behavior, which probes perception and understanding of others (action perception/other-related processing).

Voxelwise correlation between BOLD and perceived synchrony is a group-level whole-brain task-evoked analysis probing social perception (perceived interpersonal synchrony); global and local criteria satisfied.
This analysis correlates BOLD with perceived synchrony, not with affiliation/attachment ratings. Missing local inclusion criterion: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

The analysis targets perceived synchrony and does not specifically measure social communication exchanges or communicative behavior. Missing local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.

Although some regions (e.g., vmPFC) may be interpreted in self-related terms elsewhere, this voxelwise correlation is focused on perceived synchrony of the partner rather than explicit self-related judgments. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
The analysis directly probes participants' perception of partner synchrony (a form of perception/understanding of others' actions), satisfying local and global criteria.
Voxelwise negative correlations between BOLD and perceived synchrony are whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses probing social perception; global and local inclusion criteria are met.
This analysis reports correlations with perceived synchrony rather than affiliation/attachment ratings. Missing local inclusion criterion: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Analysis focuses on perceived synchrony and associated neural correlates, not on social communication per se. Missing local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
The analysis examines neural correlates of perceived synchrony of the partner rather than explicit self-related measures. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Negative correlations with perceived synchrony index participants' processing of others' behavior (action perception/mental-state inference), meeting global and local inclusion criteria.
Voxelwise correlations between BOLD and affiliation ratings are whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses directly related to social processing (affiliation). Global and local criteria satisfied.
This analysis explicitly correlates BOLD with behavioral ratings of feelings of affiliation (affiliation/attachment), satisfying both global inclusion and the local affiliation criteria.
Although affiliation is social, this analysis specifically targets affiliation ratings rather than measures of social communication; missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
The analysis examines neural correlates of affiliation toward a partner and does not include explicit self-judgment or self-related task contrasts. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Correlating BOLD with affiliation ratings toward partners indexes perception/understanding of others (including social evaluation and trait inference), meeting global and local criteria.

Whole-brain, group-level fMRI contrasts of social reputation (positive vs neutral) measure social processing (pleasantness in response to social feedback).

The task assesses reception of social reputation (pleasantness) but does not measure affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., kinship, close relationships, cooperation); missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Participants receive verbal social feedback (reputation) paired with faces, a form of social communication reception; contrasts measure this process at the whole-brain level.
Participants evaluate comments about themselves (self-referential pleasantness), so contrasts index perception/understanding of the self.
Stimuli present others' faces and their evaluations (reputation), engaging perception/understanding of others (source of social feedback) in whole-brain contrasts.
Whole-brain, group-level fMRI contrasts of social reputation (negative vs neutral) measure social processing (pleasantness/unpleasantness in response to social feedback).

The task assesses reception of social reputation but does not target affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., kinship, close relationships); missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Participants receive verbal social feedback (negative comments) with faces; the contrast captures reception of social communication at the whole-brain level.
Negative comments are directed at the participant (self-referential), so the contrast indexes self-perception and evaluation processes.
The contrast involves processing others' evaluations (faces and negative comments), engaging perception/understanding of others as sources of reputation.
Inclusive mask of (Positive>Neutral) and (Negative>Neutral) identifies regions responsive to social reputation generally, meeting social processing criteria in a whole-brain group map.

The inclusive-mask analysis identifies valence-independent reputation processing but does not target affiliation/attachment constructs; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
The conjunction of positive and negative reputation responses reflects reception of socially communicated evaluations (faces + comments) in whole-brain contrasts.
Conjunction identifies regions involved in processing reputational comments about the self regardless of valence, consistent with self-perception processes.
The analysis interrogates perception of others as sources of reputation (faces and comments) and thus involves perception/understanding of others.
The contrast (Positive vs Neutral) vs (Negative vs Neutral) isolates neural substrates specifically related to positive social reputation, a social processing measure in a whole-brain group analysis.
This contrast isolates valence-specific reputation processing but does not probe affiliation/attachment constructs per se; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
This contrast examines differential responses to socially communicated positive vs negative reputational comments (faces + sentences), fitting social communication criteria.
The contrast contrasts self-directed positive vs negative reputational comments (relative to neutral), indexing self-perception/value-related self-processing.
By comparing positive vs negative reputational input from others (relative to neutral), this contrast engages perception/understanding of others as sources of social value.

The contrast (Negative vs Neutral) vs (Positive vs Neutral) would index regions more engaged by negative reputation processing, a social processing contrast in whole-brain group analysis (even if null in results).
This analysis targets valence-specific reputation effects but does not assess affiliation/attachment constructs; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
This contrast examines differential responses to socially communicated negative vs positive reputational comments, meeting social communication criteria at the whole-brain level.
The contrast isolates neural responses to negative (vs positive) comments directed at the self (relative to neutral), consistent with self-perception processes.
Contrasting negative vs positive reputation from others probes perception of others as sources of evaluative information, engaging perception/understanding of others.

The SELF vs high-level baseline is a group-level, task-evoked whole-brain contrast in healthy adults assessing empathy-related social processing (emotional perspective taking). Meets global inclusion and local social processing criteria.
Task does not measure affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., kinship, cooperation/competition, loved one vs stranger). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
SELF-task focuses on one's own emotional response rather than reception/production of facial communication; does not meet SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1/I2.
SELF vs baseline directly measures perception/understanding of one's own emotional state in a group-level whole-brain contrast in healthy adults.
Contrast indexes self-related emotional attribution, not perception/understanding of others. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.

The OTHER vs high-level baseline contrast is a group-level, task-evoked whole-brain map in healthy adults measuring social processing (evaluation of others' emotional states). Meets global and local criteria.
The OTHER-task does not probe affiliation/attachment (e.g., kinship, loved one vs stranger). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
OTHER vs baseline measures reception of facial communication (evaluation of a face's emotional state) at the group whole-brain level in healthy adults, meeting social communication criteria.
OTHER-task targets perception of others, not self-related judgments. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
OTHER vs baseline explicitly measures perception/understanding of others' emotional states in a healthy adult group-level whole-brain contrast.

Group-level whole-brain task contrast of masked facial emotions in healthy adults directly measures social processing (perception of others' emotional expressions).

This analysis is a main effect contrast (masked sad > neutral) and does not test affiliation/attachment (no attachment-related predictor or contrast). Missing required local inclusion criteria AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
The contrast assesses reception of facial emotional communication (masked sad vs neutral) in a healthy adult sample at the group level.
The task measures perception of others' facial emotions, not self-related perception or self-judgment. Missing required local inclusion criteria PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Contrast measures perception/understanding of others' emotional states (masked emotional faces) in healthy adults at the group level.
Group-level whole-brain task contrast of masked happy vs neutral faces in healthy adults measures social processing of facial emotion.

This analysis is a main effect contrast (masked happy > neutral) and does not directly test affiliation/attachment (no attachment-related predictor). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
The contrast indexes reception of facial emotional communication (happy faces) and meets social communication criteria at the group level.
Task examines perception of others' facial emotions rather than self-related processes. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Contrast measures perception/understanding of others' emotional expressions (happy faces) in healthy adults at the group level.
Group-level voxelwise regression relating attachment avoidance to brain response to masked sad faces assesses social processing modulation by an attachment trait in healthy adults.
This analysis explicitly tests the relationship between attachment avoidance (RSQ) and brain responses to masked sad faces, meeting affiliation/attachment criteria.
Analysis assesses modulation of reception of facial communication (sad faces) by attachment avoidance, satisfying social communication criteria.

Although the analysis uses an individual-difference predictor (attachment), the task measures perception of others' emotions, not self-related perception. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
The regression assesses perception/understanding of others' emotional states (responses to sad faces) as modulated by attachment, meeting perception-of-others criteria.
Voxelwise regression of attachment avoidance with brain responses to masked happy faces evaluates social processing modulation by attachment in healthy adults.
This analysis directly tests relationships between attachment avoidance and brain responses to happy faces, fulfilling affiliation/attachment inclusion criteria.
Analysis measures reception of facial emotional communication (happy faces) and its modulation by attachment avoidance, meeting social communication criteria.
Task concerns perception of others' expressions rather than self-awareness or self-evaluation. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
The correlation examines perception/understanding of others' emotions (responses to happy faces) as modulated by attachment, satisfying perception-of-others criteria.
Voxelwise regression (negative correlations) relating attachment avoidance to brain responses to masked happy faces evaluates social processing in healthy adults.
This analysis tests correlations between attachment avoidance and brain responses to happy faces (negative correlations reported), meeting affiliation/attachment criteria.
Analysis addresses reception of facial emotional communication (happy faces) and how it relates to attachment avoidance, satisfying social communication inclusion.
This analysis focuses on perception of others' emotions (happy faces) rather than self-related perception; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Negative correlations reported reflect modulation of perception/understanding of others' emotions by attachment avoidance, meeting perception-of-others criteria.

Group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps from a dyadic eye-contact task assessing social interaction and related networks — meets global healthy adult sample and whole-brain map criteria and local social-processing criteria.

Task is eye-contact/dyadic interaction but does not specifically manipulate or contrast affiliation/attachment (no kinship, cooperation/competition, or loved-vs-stranger contrast). Missing local inclusion criteria AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
The analyses measure eye contact and gaze-related communication (reception/production of facial/eye cues) using group whole-brain task maps; meets global and local social-communication criteria.

Although the endogenous map is discussed in relation to DMN/self-referential processes, the task does not explicitly probe self-related judgments or self-perception. Missing local inclusion criteria PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Analyses probe perception/understanding of others (mentalization and empathy networks during reciprocal eye contact) with group whole-brain task maps — satisfies global and local perception-of-others criteria.

Group-level whole-brain task fMRI in healthy adults; stories present social, precautionary, and descriptive rules about people, so the contrast reflects social processing during story interpretation.

The Stories>Rest contrast is not specifically testing affiliation/attachment (e.g., cooperation, kinship, or close-relationship distinctions). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

The contrast is a broad stories>rest map and does not specifically target social communication constructs as defined (no reception/production facial or communicative contrasts). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
The task contrasts do not measure self-related perception or self-knowledge judgments. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Stories present and interpret others' behavior and rules (including social-exchange and descriptive rules about people); the Stories>Rest contrast captures processing about others’ behaviors/mental-state-relevant content.

Group whole-brain Rest>Stories contrast derived from runs with social/precaution/descriptive story stimuli; the map highlights task-related deactivations relative to rest tied to social-task engagement and is therefore relevant to social processing.
Rest>Stories does not specifically probe affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., cooperation vs non-cooperation contrasts). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

This contrast reflects relative activation during rest and is not a dedicated social-communication task contrast (no explicit communicative reception/production contrasts). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-related judgments or measures are indexed by this Rest>Stories contrast. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Rest>Stories shows greater activity at rest in regions (e.g., medial PFC/cingulate) implicated in representing others’ mental states; because the experiments involve social story stimuli, this contrast is informative about perception/understanding of others.

Card responses are part of the Wason tasks probing social-exchange, precautionary, and descriptive rules about people; the Cards>Rest contrast reflects task-evoked processing of socially-relevant decision events.

Card-phase contrasts do not specifically operationalize affiliation/attachment (no cooperation vs non-cooperation or kinship contrasts). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Card responses reflect decision-making about rule violations, not explicit social-communication reception/production contrasts. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No measures of self-related perception or self-knowledge are indexed in the Cards>Rest contrast. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

The Cards>Rest activations were mainly dorsolateral PFC, parietal, and visual regions related to decision processes; the card-phase did not robustly engage ToM/other-perception regions overall. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2 for this contrast.
Rest>Cards is derived from social-task runs and reveals relative activation at rest vs card decision events from social-task contexts; therefore relevant to social processing interpretations.
The contrast does not probe affiliation/attachment-specific constructs (no cooperation/kinship contrasts). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Rest>Cards is not a dedicated social-communication contrast (no facial/communicative reception or production measures). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-related measures are isolated by Rest>Cards. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Rest>Cards shows increased activity in medial prefrontal/cingulate areas (default/ToM-related) relative to card decision events drawn from social-task runs, so it is informative about perception/processing of others in the experiment.
Stories: Social Contracts > Precautions is a direct content contrast testing social-exchange (cheater detection/ToM) vs precautionary reasoning; this is squarely a social-processing measure.
Social contract stories explicitly probe social-exchange/cooperation and cheater detection, constructs directly related to affiliation/attachment (cooperative social bonds).
Interpreting social-exchange stories requires inferring communicative intent and socially-relevant information exchange (who benefits/requirements), fitting social communication constructs.
This contrast targets inference about others' desires/intentions (ToM/social exchange), not self-related perception or self-knowledge. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Social contract stories activated anterior/posterior temporal and posterior cingulate areas associated with inferring others’ mental states; this contrast explicitly indexes understanding mental states of others.
Stories: Social Contracts > Descriptives compares social-exchange interpretation to descriptive social rules; it isolates social-processing specific to social exchange and ToM-related inference.
This contrast isolates social-exchange / cheater-detection processes (cooperation-related), which map onto affiliation/attachment constructs (cooperative relationships).
Interpreting social contracts vs descriptives involves inferring communicative/social intent and agent-centered information exchange; thus it meets social communication criteria.
Contrast focuses on others’ desires/intentions (ToM/social exchange) rather than self-perception or self-knowledge. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Social Contracts>Descriptives engaged anterior temporal cortices implicated in understanding others’ mental states; the contrast explicitly measures perception/understanding of others.

Stories: Precautions > Social Contracts compares interpretation of precautionary rules to social-exchange rules; precautionary reasoning concerns social behavior (risk management) and thus relates to social processing.
Precautionary>Social Contract contrast targets hazard-management/risk processing rather than affiliation/cooperation per se. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Precautionary interpretation does not primarily index social-communication constructs (not a communicative intent or facial/gaze exchange contrast). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
This contrast indexes precaution interpretation about hazards and does not probe self-related perception or self-knowledge. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Authors report that precautionary stories did not activate typical ToM areas and were interpreted without inferring others’ desires/intentions; therefore PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/I2 are not met for this contrast.

Stories: Precautions > Descriptives contrasts two types of social-rule content (precautionary vs descriptive); precaution stories concern others’ behavior in hazardous contexts and thus relate to social processing.
This contrast is about hazard/precaution interpretation, not affiliation/cooperation-specific constructs. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Precaution>Descriptive is not a social-communication-specific contrast (no communicative signal reception/production). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-related perception or self-knowledge measures are isolated in this contrast. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Authors report precautionary story interpretation did not engage typical ToM/other-mental-state regions, so the contrast does not meet PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/I2.

Cards: Precautions > Social Contracts compares violation-detection for precautionary vs social-exchange cards; both involve judgments about people’s behavior in social scenarios and thus index social processing.

The card-phase precaution>social contract contrast targets hazard-violation detection rather than affiliation/cooperation-specific processes. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Card-phase contrasts here index decision-related processing about violations rather than explicit social-communication constructs (no communicative reception/production). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-related perception or self-knowledge judgments are targeted in this card-phase contrast. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

The Cards: Precautions>Social Contracts contrast showed activations in middle/posterior temporal regions (reported as including BA 21/41), which the authors note can be a neural correlate of ToM; thus this card-phase contrast includes processing related to understanding others’ states.

Cards: Precautions > Descriptives contrasts precaution violation-detection with descriptive violation-detection; both involve judgments about people’s actions in social contexts and thus relate to social processing.
This card-phase contrast indexes hazard/danger detection rather than affiliation/cooperation-specific constructs. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Contrast reflects decision-related processes for precaution vs descriptive cards, not explicit social-communication reception/production measures. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-perception or self-knowledge measures are isolated in this cards contrast. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

The authors report precaution>descriptive card activations in pre/postcentral and visual regions related to sensorimotor/decision processes rather than robust ToM/other-perception areas; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/I2 are not met.

Descriptive>Precaution contrasts do not specifically index affiliation/attachment constructs (no cooperation/kinship contrasts). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Cards: Descriptives>Social Contracts produced activations in dorsomedial/dorsolateral PFC and cingulate linked to deliberative reasoning, not clear engagement of ToM/other-perception regions; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/I2 are not met.

Cards: Descriptives > Precautions contrasts decision-related processing for descriptive vs precaution cards; both concern judgments about people’s behavior and are therefore social-processing relevant.
This cards contrast indexes deliberative decision processes rather than affiliation/attachment-specific constructs. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
